name: meinMPP
description: The German company-bike scheme (Dienstrad) applied to iPhones, tablets and laptops. The employer signs a master leasing agreement and sets budgets, and staff order hardware and pay through gross-salary conversion, saving up to ~30% depending on tax bracket (founder-stated). Converting €250/month of gross salary buys roughly €4,000–5,000 of hardware (founder-stated). Homepage: "Private Wunschtechnik ~30 % günstiger per Gehaltsumwandlung", "Über 250+ Unternehmen vertrauen bereits auf meinMPP", free for employers (company-stated). Managing director Dominik Albers is the only employee; the platform is built in-house on Laravel + Filament (founder-stated).

mentions.evidence: Order volume has doubled on average every year since the January 2022 launch (founder-stated) Planning at least €2.1–2.4 million for 2026, the first year the company turns a profit (founder-stated forecast) Apple is 75–80% of order volume (founder-stated) Note: not Stripe-verified; it's a forecast, and the write-up doesn't say whether the figure is revenue or order volume.
mentions.indieAngle: Poland has no Dienstrad-style tax break, but the plumbing pattern carries over: a white-label benefits/leasing portal sold through leasing companies and payroll providers, where you own the HR workflow and the partner owns the balance sheet. Alternatively, build the payroll-export/HR glue that German MPP/Dienstrad providers all need.

whyItPrints: Payroll and tax-benefit plumbing. Employers configure the payroll export once, then only approve joiners and remove leavers ("one customer with 200 contracts budgets half an hour a month", founder-stated). The margin comes at the end: ~1% on iPhones up front, but after 24 months almost 90% of staff buy the device at residual value and ~70% reorder right away (founder-stated). More than half of enquiries come from a partner network of benefits platforms, leasing firms and distributors (founder-stated).
